newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Bond industry calls for euro debt conventions.
newsitem.headline: Bond industry calls for euro debt conventions.

text.p: A group of securities industry associations said on Thursday the bond market should adopt conventions for trading euro-denominated bonds to prevent disruption once the single currency is introduced.

Delegates at the International Securities Market Association (ISMA) annual general meeting were told there was a seeming lack of desire by politically motivated domestic markets to implement such conventions, crucial for the trading of debt once Europan economic and monetary union (EMU) is completed. This is scheduled for January 1, 1999.

"The recommendations would promote liquidity and transparency, prevent confusion and disputes for euro trading and settlement and establish a basis for standard market practice for the single currency," John Dowsett, chairman of ISMA's market practices committee, said.
The market conventions are as follows:
- Accrued interest should be calculated on an actual/actual day count basis,
- Coupon payments should be made on an annual basis,
- A business day should be a day when Cedel Bank, Euroclear and TARGET are open for business and should be kept to a maximum,
- Transactions should continue to be settled three business days following the trade date, and it is not appropriate to shorten this time immediately,
- Trades in amounts with fractions should be expressed in decimals rather than fractions.

"We are confident these new market conventions are an important milestone in securing the continuing uniformity and harmony in the international securities market, if, as and when the European single currency will be introduced," Dowsett said.
The International Primary Market Association (IPMA) supports all the conventions, but the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) has called for a semi-annual coupon for euro debt.
"Our feeling is the derivatives market should follow the cash market, but harmony in this area is not as compelling as in other matters," Dowsett said.
